action.recommendation: Ensure your repository has a comprehensive .gitignore file. Include: build artifacts, dependency directories (node_modules, venv), secrets and .env files, IDE configuration, OS metadata (.DS_Store, Thumbs.db), and log files. Use gitignore.io to generate a baseline.

rationale: Missing .gitignore leads to committed secrets, binary files, and machine-specific configuration that pollutes the repository.

description: Use environment variables for all configuration secrets

action.recommendation: Store all secrets, API keys, and environment-specific configuration in environment variables, never in source code. Use .env files locally (gitignored), document required environment variables in .env.example, and use a secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault) in production.

rationale: Hardcoded secrets in source code are the most common cause of credential exposure. Environment variables separate configuration from code.

description: Every repository should have a README

action.recommendation: Create a README.md for your repository. At minimum include: project name and description, installation instructions, usage examples, contributing guidance, and license. A good README is the first impression of your project.

rationale: A README is the universal entry point for any code repository. Its absence signals an unmaintained or inaccessible project.

description: Include a LICENSE file in all repositories

action.recommendation: Add a LICENSE file to your repository. If the project is internal and proprietary, use a confidential notice. If open source, choose an appropriate OSS license. The absence of a license defaults to all rights reserved, which may not be your intent.

rationale: Every code repository needs a license to clarify usage rights. Unlicensed code creates legal ambiguity for contributors and users.

description: Enforce consistent code style with tooling

action.recommendation: Add automated code style enforcement to your project. Use a linter (ESLint, pylint, golint) and formatter (Prettier, Black, gofmt). Configure rules, add pre-commit hooks (husky, pre-commit), and run style checks in CI. Agree on and document style decisions in a contributing guide.

rationale: Consistent code style reduces cognitive load in code review, enabling reviewers to focus on logic rather than formatting.
